body: I feel we miss a test for the getConfiguration order? (__initLast true/false)
You can safely use Date.now() everywhere, will be polyfill`ed: https://cdn.polyfill.io/v1/docs/features/#Date_now
Same thing, you can use addEventListener everywhere, polyfill takes care of it
Why 2 underscores? To denote that it's `private` but not directly used by the instance?
Should we make all of these properties "private"? So that the user inspecting our object will see on what he can or cannot rely (even if he should not rely on anything here).
Either this or we do not return anything for now.
You can use default params and destructuring like in other widgets for this usage.

Why do we need to trigger a blur on every input?

I fear this could trigger some weird behaviors if there are some event listeners on blur() on any input we do not control (rendering, animation, ..)
Because React https://reactjs.algolia.com/docs/forms.html
Thanks!

body: Will add one
Sorry can you precise a little bit more the real issue (= what happens if we do not blur every input?)

I read some github issues on components about polyfill and addEventListener that's why I went for that. If we are polyfilling they it makes that useless because we won't be able to feature detect anything... Are you sure it correctly changes the name of the event?

it's not private since it is used by the InstantSearch.js. But that's an hidden feature sure. And one that we wouldn't want anyone else to use. I would be interested in other solutions for that... (maybe we could do some type detection since it's now a Class)
Yes you can rely on the polyfill for this https://github.com/Financial-Times/polyfill-service/blob/master/polyfills/Event/polyfill-ie8.js#L88
Seems like we can use symbol to define private properties. I could do that...
ok
yep!
It's a good solution, other solutions would be to inherit from "LateWidget" and check instanceof LateWidget which in the end is exactly the same effect with more wrapping..

> it's not private since it is used by the InstantSearch.js

Yes sorry when I say "private" it's always from the API user POV.

I am interested because I do not know anything about Symbol (or the use case).

The only thing I would like to do right now is hide or _prefix properties that will be passed to the api user. And right now there's no way for him to understand that it's somehow "private"

To be able to update the value of an input programmatically you need to have a controlled component. But then we only render on the search result, which introduce a lot of lag and therefore inconsistencies during the input of the search box. The solution I found here is to make a mixed controlled/uncontrolled component. The component is fully controlled when not focus and uncontrolled when focus. But then when you do a back you have to be able to change the value, therefore you need it to be blurred beforehand hence we have to do that.

One other solution would be to be able to render when the `change` event occur in the helper. This way we could only render on the change and not on results. I can try that. What do you think?
But it's visible... only if someone looks at the source code. And I would trust someone who make the effort to read the code.
Cool :)
Ok let's postpone "private" and "public" stuff untill we have methods on widget instances (like .on).
